title: OML record
description: One misconception in the Open Misconception Library. Schema version 0.2 (v0.1.1 release): framework-agnostic alignments, reviews[] with a status lifecycle, computed trust.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor support.

id.description: Stable, human-readable ID. Lowercase, dot-separated; the first segment is the domain. Never reused.

uuid.description: Opaque identifier, unique across the library. Used as the CASE CFItem identifier.

version.description: Semantic version of this record's content. Bump patch for wording, minor for added evidence, major for a changed statement.

status.description: Lifecycle: draft -> llm-reviewed -> reviewed -> deprecated | merged. llm-reviewed needs at least one model review with verdict accept covering statement and evidence; reviewed needs at least one human accept or one attested review. merged requires history.merged_into. The validator enforces the review rules.

title.description: Short label for the misconception, a noun phrase.

statement.description: The belief, stated as the learner would hold it. A belief, not a wrong answer.

kind.description: Mechanism by which the belief arises.

domain.description: Subject area, matching the first segment of `id` (e.g. `math`, `prog`). May be qualified (`math.fractions`).

about.description: Concepts this misconception is about: {scheme, uri, code?, note?}. scheme is a free string; known schemes live in schemes/registry.json and the validator warns on unknown ones. Prefer CASE item URIs; use OML concept URIs (<base>/c/<id>) only where no CASE URI exists.

level_band.description: Education levels where the misconception is typically observed.

locale.description: BCP 47 tag for the language of `statement` and examples. Default `en`.

evidence_patterns.description: Observable response patterns that indicate the belief. At least one, each with a concrete example.

discriminators.description: How to tell this misconception apart from a slip and from its nearest neighbours.

vs_slip.description: What distinguishes a systematic holder of this belief from someone who made a one-off error.

vs.description: Keyed by neighbouring OML id; value explains the observable difference.

relations.description: Typed links. Closed object, decided 2026-09-05: conflicts_with and resolved_by point at Concepts (external URIs, or OML concept URIs); confusable_with and specializes point at OML misconception records. confusable_with is symmetric; the validator warns when the reverse edge is missing. The record id/uri is the canonical public ID of the corresponding Knowledge Map Misconception node; there is no second identifier field.

resolved_by.description: Concepts whose understanding corrects this belief.

confusable_with.description: Misconceptions that produce similar evidence and need a discriminator. Symmetric.

specializes.description: Broader misconceptions of which this is a special case.

alignments.description: Links to items in external schemes: {scheme, uri, code?, note?}. Framework-agnostic; see schemes/registry.json.

provenance.description: Where this record's claim comes from.

origin.description: How the record entered OML. `llm-drafted` records must cite literature in `sources` and stay `draft` until reviewed.

prevalence.description: Reserved for measured prevalence. Out of scope for v1; shape is provisional.

merged_into.description: Required when status is `merged`. The surviving record.

license.description: Licence for this record's content. All OML records are CC BY 4.0.

notes.description: Free text about the record that is not part of the belief itself, e.g. likely origins of the misconception.

trust.description: Computed by `oml trust` from reviews[] against reviewers/registry.json. Never hand-typed; the validator fails on a stored value that does not match the computed one.

reviews.description: Reviews of this record. Each entry records who reviewed what, when, and with which verdict. Human reviewers carry a durable handle; model reviewers carry a model id and version; attested reviews point at the provenance source that asserts the misconception.

disputed.description: True while an open dispute challenges this record. A disputed record stays live and citable; the site and the JSON show the flag and link the issues. Set by a maintainer when a dispute is accepted for ruling; see GOVERNANCE.md.

disputes.description: URLs of dispute issues raised against this record, open or settled. Entries are never removed: a settled dispute stays as part of the record's history.

item_shape.description: The kind of task on which the pattern shows (e.g. `add two fractions with unlike denominators`).

signature.description: The response rule a holder of the belief follows, stated so a grader could apply it.

item.description: The task as shown to the learner.

response.description: The response a holder of the belief gives.

scheme.description: Name of the scheme, e.g. CASE, OML, CCSS, progmiscon. Free string; not an enum.

code.description: Human-readable code in the scheme (e.g. 5.NF.A.1, Java/AssignCompares).

relation.description: How this record relates to the item. Default about.

identifier.description: The source's own identifier for this misconception, if any.

license.description: Licence of the source, if text was reused.

external.description: A CASE item URI, or an OML concept URI (<base>/c/<concept-id>), or another external concept URI.

by.description: human: name plus a durable handle, e.g. "Vikram Maram (github:vikram-learnco)" or an ORCID. model: model id and version, e.g. claude-fable-5-1. attested: integer index into provenance.sources[] of the source asserting the misconception.

date.description: For model reviews this pins the model's capability at review time.
